key_insight: CalTennis introduces a very large real-world tennis video benchmark for testing monocular-to-3D pose estimation under challenging in-the-wild conditions. It provides synchronized multi-view video at scale, making it possible to evaluate 3D pose methods more rigorously than before.
problem_solved: Existing datasets for monocular-to-3D pose estimation are either too small, lack real-world diversity, or do not provide enough synchronized multi-view ground truth. This paper addresses the need for a large, sports-specific benchmark with high-quality multi-camera captures.
method: Collected 11M+ frames (51 hours) of tennis practice and match play from 40 players.
Captured each session with 2-6 synchronized cameras at 60 Hz to enable multi-view evaluation.
Created a benchmark focused on monocular-to-3D pose estimation in unconstrained, real-world sports settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CalTennis offers a much stronger testbed for evaluating pose estimation models in realistic motion and viewpoint conditions. It can help reveal failure modes that smaller or less diverse datasets miss, leading to more robust 3D human pose systems.

paper_title: CalTennis: Large Multi-View Tennis Video Dataset and Benchmark of Monocular-to-3D Pose Estimation
paper_authors: Ilona Demler, Xinran Xie, Blake Werner, Anna Szczuka, Pietro Perona
